title: Cap. 7 Patrum: Ambrose — suffered for all, specially for the Church
pass_a_gloss: 4. A fourth testimony can be sought from Ambrose, whose words are these: And Christ suffered for all, yet for us he suffered specially, because he suffered for the Church. And so there is no doubt that she owes more who has received more — book 6, chapter 7 on Luke. Here we see that, in Ambrose's mind, there was a special regard of the suffering Christ toward his Church, whence it came about that she received a special fruit from Christ's passion. He therefore affirms that Christ suffered for all in such a way that nevertheless the will and intention of the suffering Christ does not look upon all equally, but is borne in a certain singular manner upon his mystical body, that is, the Church of the firstborn, which by his blood he willed to acquire for himself, and by the Spirit to join to an unfrustrating participation of eternal life. He did not suffer for all with this special intention.
pass_b_english: 4. Ambrose supplies a fourth witness: And Christ suffered for all, yet for us he suffered specially, because he suffered for the Church. So she who received more doubtless owes more (On Luke, book 6, chapter 7). On Ambrose's reading, the suffering Christ had a special regard for his Church, and from that she drew a special fruit of the passion. He can say Christ suffered for all, and still hold that the will and intention of the suffering Christ does not regard everyone alike, but turns in a singular way upon his mystical body — the Church of the firstborn — which he meant by his blood to make his own and by the Spirit to join to a share in eternal life that cannot fail. He did not suffer for all under that special intention.
source_text: 4. Quartum testimonium ex Ambrosio peti potest, cujus haec sunt verba, Et Christus passus est pro omnibus, pro nobis tamen specialiter passus est, quia pro Ecclesia passus est. Itaque non est dubium quod plus debeat quae plus accepit, lib. 6. cap. 7. Lucae. Hic videmus ex mente Ambrosii fuisse specialem Christi patientis ad Ecclesiam suam intuitum, unde factum est ut ea ex passione Christi specialem fructum perceperit. Ita igitur Christum pro omnibus passum asserit, ut tamen voluntas & intentio Christi patientis haud omnes ex aequo respiciat, sed singulari quodam modo feratur in corpus suum mysticum, id est, primogenitorum Ecclesiam, quam sanguine suo voluit sibi acquirere, Spiritu conjungere ad infrustrabilem vitae aeternae participationem. Non passus est pro omnibus speciali hac intentione.
